---
title: "GNSS Station Positions"
---

```{R}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
devtools::load_all("~/Documents/Research/Code/ECE")
library(tidyverse)
library(kableExtra)
library(psych)
```

Daily GNSS station positions from the Jet Propulsion Laboratory (`sideshow.jpl.nasa.gov/pub/JPL_GPS_Timeseries/repro2018a/post/point/`, one `.series` file per station). The stations and window follow the application in Collilieux, Lebarbier and Robin, *A factor model approach for the joint segmentation with between-series correlation* ([arXiv:1505.05660](https://arxiv.org/abs/1505.05660)). Like that paper, we analyze differences from `MPLE`, not the raw station series.

Five stations in Michigan and Ohio, less than 250 km apart: `ADRI`, `BAYR`, `BRIG`, `DEFI` and `MPLE`. We use the east component from March 2002 to June 2013, in mm.

Why correlation is expected: nearby stations see the same ground deformation, atmosphere and correlated processing errors, so their noise should be positively correlated.

Why the mean is non-stationary: the North American plate moves about -16 mm/yr in this component, so every series is a steep, nearly linear trend that is shared across stations. On top of that, receiver and antenna changes cause sudden jumps in a single station's recorded position. Naive Pearson correlation on the raw levels picks up the shared trend and is close to 1 for every pair. To remove it, every analysis from here on uses the four differences station minus `MPLE`, so a label such as `ADRI` in the text means `ADRI-MPLE`, and tables carry the full names. The differences have piecewise-constant means with no trend, which is the setting ECE is built for. Because all four share `-MPLE`, part of their between-series correlation comes from `MPLE`'s own noise and jumps, so the question tested is correlation between the differences, not between the original stations.

```{R}
#| echo: false
#| label: gnss-load

read_series <- function(station) {
  read.table(
    sprintf("../data/real-data/gnss/%s.series", station),
    col.names = c("decyear", "east", "north", "up", "sig_e", "sig_n", "sig_u",
                  "cor_en", "cor_eu", "cor_nu", "j2000", "yr", "mo", "day",
                  "hr", "min", "sec")
  ) |>
    mutate(date = as.Date(sprintf("%d-%02d-%02d", yr, mo, day)),
           station = station, east = 1000 * east) |>
    group_by(station, date) |>
    summarise(east = mean(east), .groups = "drop")
}

stations <- c("ADRI", "BAYR", "BRIG", "DEFI", "MPLE")

X_raw <- map(stations, read_series) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  filter(date >= "2002-03-01", date <= "2013-06-30") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = station, values_from = east) |>
  filter(complete.cases(pick(everything()))) |>
  arrange(date)

X_mat <- X_raw |> select(all_of(stations)) |> as.matrix()

win <- 25
roll_mat <- apply(X_mat, 2, function(col) rolling_mean(col, win))
colnames(roll_mat) <- colnames(X_mat)
```

The data covers days on which all five stations report: `r nrow(X_mat)` of about 4,100 days, so roughly 6% of days are missing. The first weeks of 2002 are dropped because the series start with a short transient. Same-day observations are averaged.

Known equipment changes, from Table 2 of the paper. All are receiver changes except where noted.

```{R table-gnss-events}
#| echo: false

tribble(
  ~Station, ~`Known changes`,
  "ADRI", "2004-12-02, 2005-09-15, 2006-08-02",
  "BAYR", "2004-12-02, 2005-08-31, 2006-07-11",
  "BRIG", "2004-12-02, 2005-09-12, 2008-04-14 (antenna)",
  "DEFI", "2006-10-11 (antenna), 2009-04-07, 2011-01-26, 2012-08-02 (antenna), 2012-11-05 (antenna)",
  "MPLE", "2004-12-02, 2005-09-14, 2006-12-28, 2007-05-08 (receiver and antenna), 2007-10-05"
) |>
  kable(align = c("l", "l")) |>
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)
```

## Full Resolution

::: {.panel-tabset}

## Plot

The paper subtracts `MPLE` from the other four stations, which cancels the shared plate motion and leaves the jumps (its Figure 7). This plot is the same view, with the known equipment changes marked. Red dotted lines are `MPLE` events, which appear in every difference. Blue dashed lines are the other station's own events. The black line is the fitted piecewise-constant mean from `segment_mean(penalty = "BIC")`, applied to each difference separately. The other tabs use the same differences.

```{R plot-gnss-diff}
#| echo: false

own_events <- tribble(
  ~station, ~date,
  "ADRI", "2004-12-02", "ADRI", "2005-09-15", "ADRI", "2006-08-02",
  "BAYR", "2004-12-02", "BAYR", "2005-08-31", "BAYR", "2006-07-11",
  "BRIG", "2004-12-02", "BRIG", "2005-09-12", "BRIG", "2008-04-14",
  "DEFI", "2006-10-11", "DEFI", "2009-04-07", "DEFI", "2011-01-26",
  "DEFI", "2012-08-02", "DEFI", "2012-11-05"
) |>
  mutate(date = as.Date(date), series = paste0(station, "-MPLE"))

mple_events <- as.Date(c("2004-12-02", "2005-09-14", "2006-12-28",
                         "2007-05-08", "2007-10-05"))

# The four MPLE differences and their segmented means (shared by the Plot and
# Residuals tabs).
gnss_diff_seg <- function(X, penalty = "BIC") {
  D <- cbind(`ADRI-MPLE` = X[, "ADRI"] - X[, "MPLE"],
             `BAYR-MPLE` = X[, "BAYR"] - X[, "MPLE"],
             `BRIG-MPLE` = X[, "BRIG"] - X[, "MPLE"],
             `DEFI-MPLE` = X[, "DEFI"] - X[, "MPLE"])
  D_seg <- segment_mean(D, penalty = penalty)
  colnames(D_seg) <- colnames(D)
  list(D = D, D_seg = D_seg)
}

plot_gnss_diff <- function(dates, X, penalty = "BIC") {
  seg <- gnss_diff_seg(X, penalty)
  D <- seg$D
  D_seg <- seg$D_seg

  to_long <- function(M, name) {
    as_tibble(M) |>
      mutate(date = dates) |>
      pivot_longer(-date, names_to = "series", values_to = name)
  }
  diff_long <- to_long(D, "mm") |>
    left_join(to_long(D_seg, "fit"), by = c("date", "series"))

  ggplot(diff_long, aes(date, mm)) +
    geom_line(color = "gray55", linewidth = 0.25) +
    geom_line(aes(y = fit), color = "black", linewidth = 0.6) +
    geom_vline(data = expand_grid(series = unique(diff_long$series), date = mple_events),
               aes(xintercept = date), color = "red", linetype = "dotted") +
    geom_vline(data = own_events, aes(xintercept = date),
               color = "steelblue", linetype = "dashed") +
    facet_grid(series ~ ., scales = "free_y") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "East difference (mm)") +
    theme_minimal()
}

plot_gnss_diff(X_raw$date, X_mat)
```

## Residuals

Difference minus its segmented mean (the black line in the Plot tab), for each MPLE difference.

```{R resid-gnss-full}
#| echo: false

par(mfrow = c(4, 1), mar = c(0, 3, 0, 1), oma = c(4, 0, 1, 0), mgp = c(1.8, 1, 0))

seg <- gnss_diff_seg(X_mat)
for (i in 1:4) {
  resid_i <- seg$D[, i] - seg$D_seg[, i]
  plot(X_raw$date, resid_i, type = "l", xaxt = "n",
       ylab = colnames(seg$D)[i], cex.lab = 0.8)
  abline(h = 0, lty = "dotted")
}
axis.Date(1, X_raw$date)
mtext("Date", side = 1, outer = TRUE, line = 2.5)
```

<!-- STALE: these ACF numbers were computed for the raw stations; the ACF tabs now use the four MPLE differences. Recompute. -->
Residual lag-1 ACF is 0.32, 0.35, 0.33, 0.19 and 0.38 (`ADRI`, `BAYR`, `BRIG`, `DEFI`, `MPLE`). This is real short-lag dependence, but well below the 0.7 to 0.9 seen in streamflow or ocean series. The ACF is also slightly negative near lag 7 (about -0.12), a weak weekly effect. Fixed steps of 2 to 3 days bring lag 1 to about 0.1 to 0.2, and none of them divides the 7-day period.

## Kappa

The default pairwise z-test (`ece.test(..., type = "z.test")`) uses `kappa = "gaussian"`, which assumes `k40 = k04 = 3`, `k22 = 1 + 2ρ²` and `k31 = k13 = 3ρ`. We check this by estimating the terms from the segmented residuals of the four `MPLE` differences (`D_ds3`) (`ece.kappa(..., method = "mom")`, `segment_mean(penalty = "BIC")`):

```{R gnss-kappa-check}
#| echo: false

X_resid_ds3 <- D_ds3 - seg_ds3$D_seg

cn_k  <- colnames(D_ds3)
idx_k <- combn(ncol(D_ds3), 2)

kappa_tbl <- purrr::map_dfr(seq_len(ncol(idx_k)), function(k) {
  i <- idx_k[1, k]
  j <- idx_k[2, k]
  kap <- ece.kappa(X_resid_ds3[, i], X_resid_ds3[, j], method = "mom")
  tibble(
    Pair = paste(cn_k[i], "/", cn_k[j]),
    k40  = round(kap$k40, 2),
    k31  = round(kap$k31, 2),
    k22  = round(kap$k22, 2),
    k13  = round(kap$k13, 2),
    k04  = round(kap$k04, 2)
  )
})

kable(kappa_tbl, align = c("l", "c", "c", "c", "c", "c")) |>
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)
```

<!-- STALE: recompute after render -->
The marginal terms `k40` and `k04` are above 3 for every station, from about 4 to 22, and `DEFI` is the heaviest-tailed (`k04` = 22.02). The `k22` terms are above 1 for most pairs, and a few `k13` terms are negative. The Gaussian reference does not hold, so the null-restricted z-test (`rho = 0`) used in the pairwise results is the safer choice.

## Omega

$\omega_{xy} = T_1(\theta_x,\theta_y)/n$ from `omega-estimation.qmd` is the circular sum of products of the mean jumps, divided by $n$. We estimate it two ways on the four `MPLE` differences of the downsampled data (`D_ds3`).

::: {.panel-tabset}

### ECE

`ece.complexity()` computes $\omega$ directly from lagged differences, with no segmentation.

```{R gnss-omega-ece-diff}
#| echo: false

ece_omega_diff <- ece.complexity(D_ds3) |> round(4)
rownames(ece_omega_diff) <- colnames(ece_omega_diff) <- colnames(D_ds3)

knitr::kable(ece_omega_diff, caption = "ECE (no segmentation), MPLE differences")
```

### Segmentation

Here $\omega$ is computed from the jumps between adjacent segment means of `segment_mean(penalty = "BIC")`: $\hat\omega_{xy} = \frac{1}{n}\sum_i \Delta_{i,x}\Delta_{i,y}$. The circular version includes the seam jump (last segment mean minus first), as the circular lagged differences do. The non-circular version leaves it out. The two differ exactly by $(\hat\theta_{x,n}-\hat\theta_{x,1})(\hat\theta_{y,n}-\hat\theta_{y,1})/n$.

```{R gnss-omega-seg}
#| echo: false

omega_seg <- function(theta, circular = TRUE) {
  n <- nrow(theta)
  jumps <- diff(theta)
  if (circular) jumps <- rbind(jumps, theta[1, ] - theta[n, ])
  crossprod(jumps) / n
}

theta_diff <- seg_ds3$D_seg

seg_tab <- function(theta, circular, caption, digits) {
  knitr::kable(round(omega_seg(theta, circular), digits), caption = caption)
}
```

```{R gnss-omega-seg-diff-circ}
#| echo: false
seg_tab(theta_diff, TRUE, "Segmentation, MPLE differences, circular", 3)
```

```{R gnss-omega-seg-diff-noncirc}
#| echo: false
seg_tab(theta_diff, FALSE, "Segmentation, MPLE differences, non-circular", 3)
```

:::

## Size

Under H0 the p-values of a valid test are uniform. To check this on the GNSS data, we circularly shift each `MPLE` difference by an independent random offset. This keeps each series' own dynamics (jumps, serial dependence) and removes any alignment across stations, so the series are independent by construction. (Shifting breaks the shared `-MPLE` term across differences, which is the intended null.) We run each ECE-based global test on 1,000 shifted copies of `D_ds3`. The naive tests are left out.

```{R gnss-size-sim}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| cache: true

shift_cols <- function(X) {
  n <- nrow(X)
  apply(X, 2, function(x) x[((seq_len(n) + sample(n, 1)) %% n) + 1])
}

set.seed(123)
size_sim <- map_dfr(1:1000, function(b) {
  Xs <- shift_cols(D_ds3)
  tibble(
    rep = b,
    `Bootstrap Multiplier`                              = ece.test(Xs, type = "bs.multiplier")$p.value,
    `Parametric Bootstrap (Diagonal, PSD)`              = ece.test(Xs, type = "bs.parametric.lag1.diag.psd")$p.value,
    `Parametric Bootstrap (PSD)`                        = ece.test(Xs, type = "bs.parametric.psd")$p.value,
    `Parametric Bootstrap (PSD, Centered)`              = ece.test(Xs, type = "bs.parametric.psd.center")$p.value,
    `Parametric Bootstrap (PSD, Normalized)`            = ece.test(Xs, type = "bs.parametric.psd.norm")$p.value,
    `Parametric Bootstrap (PSD, Centered + Normalized)` = bs_parametric_test(Xs, force_psd = TRUE, center = TRUE, normalize = TRUE)$p.value
  )
})

size_long <- size_sim |>
  pivot_longer(-rep, names_to = "Method", values_to = "p") |>
  mutate(Method = factor(Method, levels = names(size_sim)[-1]))
```

```{R gnss-size-hist}
#| echo: false
#| label: fig-gnss-size-hist
#| fig-cap: "P-values of each ECE-based global test on 1,000 independently shifted copies of the data. A valid test has density 1 in every bin."
#| fig-height: 6

ggplot(size_long, aes(x = p)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), breaks = seq(0, 1, by = 0.1), fill = "steelblue", color = "white") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", color = "firebrick") +
  facet_wrap(~Method, ncol = 2) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(x = "p-value", y = "Density")
```

:::

Lag-1 residual ACF drops to 0.13, 0.16, 0.19, 0.08 and 0.20, with lag 2 at 0.03 to 0.09. Some dependence is left, so the p-values below should be read with that in mind.

## Results

```{R gnss-results-helpers}
#| echo: false

# Null-restricted z-test (rho = 0), as in the CPI chapter.
ece_pval_null <- function(X) {
  p <- ncol(X)
  pval_mat <- matrix(NA, p, p)
  colnames(pval_mat) <- rownames(pval_mat) <- colnames(X)
  for (i in 1:(p - 1)) {
    for (j in (i + 1):p) {
      pair <- cbind(X[, i], X[, j])
      pval <- ece.test(pair, type = "z.test", kappa = ece.kappa(pair, rho = 0, method = "mom"), rho = 0)$p.value
      pval_mat[i, j] <- pval
      pval_mat[j, i] <- pval
    }
  }
  diag(pval_mat) <- 0
  pval_mat
}

# Pairwise diagonal z-test (centered): tests the ECE covariance directly, with the
# standard error estimated from the variance of the ECE terms.
diag_pval_mat <- function(X) {
  p <- ncol(X)
  pval_mat <- matrix(NA, p, p, dimnames = list(colnames(X), colnames(X)))
  for (i in 1:(p - 1)) {
    for (j in (i + 1):p) {
      pval <- suppressWarnings(ece.test(X[, c(i, j)], type = "z.test.hac.center")$p.value)
      pval_mat[i, j] <- pval
      pval_mat[j, i] <- pval
    }
  }
  diag(pval_mat) <- 0
  pval_mat
}

# Bold any off-diagonal cell whose corresponding p-value is < 0.05.
bold_sig <- function(display_mat, pval_mat) {
  m   <- nrow(display_mat)
  out <- matrix("", m, m, dimnames = dimnames(display_mat))
  for (i in seq_len(m)) {
    for (j in seq_len(m)) {
      sig <- i != j && !is.na(pval_mat[i, j]) && pval_mat[i, j] < 0.05
      out[i, j] <- kableExtra::cell_spec(sprintf("%.3f", display_mat[i, j]), "html", bold = sig)
    }
  }
  out
}
```

```{R gnss-pairwise}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false

ece_cor <- ece.cor(D_ds3) |> round(3)
dimnames(ece_cor) <- list(colnames(D_ds3), colnames(D_ds3))

ece_cov <- ece.cov(D_ds3) |> round(3)
dimnames(ece_cov) <- list(colnames(D_ds3), colnames(D_ds3))

# Residuals after removing the BIC-segmented means (jumps removed).
R_ds3 <- D_ds3 - seg_ds3$D_seg

pw <- list(
  ece_cor      = ece_cor,
  pearson_cor  = cor(D_ds3) |> round(3),
  ece_pmat     = ece_pval_null(D_ds3) |> round(3),
  pearson_pmat = cor_pval(D_ds3) |> round(3),
  seg_cor      = cor(R_ds3) |> round(3),
  seg_pmat     = cor_pval(R_ds3) |> round(3),
  naive_cov    = cov(D_ds3) |> round(3),
  seg_cov      = cov(R_ds3) |> round(3),
  ece_cov      = ece_cov,
  diag_pmat    = diag_pval_mat(D_ds3) |> round(3)
)

set.seed(123)
bs_mult_p <- ece.test(D_ds3, type = "bs.multiplier")$p.value
bs_param_p <- ece.test(D_ds3, type = "bs.parametric.lag1.diag.psd")$p.value
bs_naive_p <- ece.test(D_ds3, type = "bs.parametric.naive")$p.value
set.seed(123)
bs_psd_p <- ece.test(D_ds3, type = "bs.parametric.psd")$p.value
set.seed(123)
bs_psd_center_p <- ece.test(D_ds3, type = "bs.parametric.psd.center")$p.value
set.seed(123)
bs_psd_norm_p <- ece.test(D_ds3, type = "bs.parametric.psd.norm")$p.value
set.seed(123)
bs_psd_cn_p <- bs_parametric_test(D_ds3, force_psd = TRUE, center = TRUE, normalize = TRUE)$p.value
bartlett_p <- cortest.bartlett(cor(D_ds3), nrow(D_ds3))$p.value

diag_res <- data.frame(
  Method = c(
    "Bootstrap Multiplier",
    "Parametric Bootstrap (Diagonal, PSD)",
    "Parametric Bootstrap (PSD)",
    "Parametric Bootstrap (PSD, Centered)",
    "Parametric Bootstrap (PSD, Normalized)",
    "Parametric Bootstrap (PSD, Centered + Normalized)",
    "Parametric Bootstrap (Naive)",
    "Bartlett Test"
  ),
  `p-value` = round(c(bs_mult_p, bs_param_p, bs_psd_p, bs_psd_center_p, bs_psd_norm_p, bs_psd_cn_p, bs_naive_p, bartlett_p), 3),
  check.names = FALSE
)

knitr::kable(bold_sig(pw$ece_cov, pw$ece_pmat),       caption = "ECE Correlation (z-test, null SE)", escape = FALSE, format = "html")
knitr::kable(bold_sig(pw$ece_cov, pw$diag_pmat),      caption = "ECE Covariance (diagonal z-test, centered)", escape = FALSE, format = "html")
```

## Diagonal

```{R gnss-diagonal-tests-output}
#| echo: false

# Bold any row with p-value < 0.05.
diag_table <- function(df, caption) {
  df[["p-value"]] <- sprintf("%.3f", df[["p-value"]])
  sig <- which(as.numeric(df[["p-value"]]) < 0.05)
  kable(df, align = c("l", "c"), row.names = FALSE, caption = caption) |>
    row_spec(sig, bold = TRUE) |>
    kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)
}

is_naive <- grepl("Naive|Bartlett", diag_res$Method)

diag_table(diag_res[!is_naive, ], "ECE-based tests (mean-shift-aware)")
diag_table(diag_res[is_naive, ],  "Naive tests (no mean-shift adjustment)")
```
